sources.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory
sources.locator: §5.1, complete decision-rule and randomized-test discussion, PDF pp. 100–102. Read the pointwise data-to-action rule, probability-measure-valued randomized rule, its Dirac special case, and the binary coin-flip interpretation. No action-space convexity guarantee is imported.

contents.name: §5.1: a statistic or estimator is a data function with an estimate at the observed value
contents.reason: The source gives the decision-rule/data-map convention; the local definition makes the source and target measurable spaces explicit and ties an estimator to a named estimand.

contents.name: §5.1, Definition 5.1: a randomized decision rule assigns a probability measure on actions to each data value
§5.1: deterministic rules are point masses and binary randomization uses a coin with data-dependent rejection probability
§5.1: measurable action-integral and induced action-law consequences
contents.reason: Martin states the action-distribution integral but does not prove measurable dependence for a general kernel. The local lemma proves measurability from increasing simple approximations and kernel evaluations, and then proves the induced action law by monotone convergence.

contents.name: Theorem 5.2, randomization-removal claim
contents.reason: Not part of this inventory. The source proof also requires convex action-space and barycenter/integrability hypotheses absent from its printed statement; no such claim is copied.

sources.title: Peter Hoff, Statistical Decision Problems
sources.locator: Complete 13-page lecture note, especially estimator definition PDF pp. 2–3, test function PDF pp. 4–5, and decision rules/action distributions PDF pp. 6–8. The later preference-representation theorem is not used.

contents.name: §2, pp. 2–3: a measurable data function is an estimator and its value is the estimate
§3, pp. 4–5: a test function takes values in [0,1] and gives the rejection probability after observing x
§§4.1–4.2, pp. 6–8: decisions may be distributions on the action space
contents.reason: Hoff's decision-distribution formulation is adapted locally to a pointwise probability kernel with an explicit action sigma-algebra and eventwise measurability.

contents.name: §5, PDF p. 10, preference-representation Theorem 1
contents.reason: The printed display repeats the same P2 expectation on both sides and is malformed. It is unrelated to the assigned definitions and supplies no claim here.

sources.title: Peter Kempthorne, MIT 18.655 Lecture Note 6: Sufficiency
sources.locator: Complete 21-page lecture unit; especially slides/PDF pp. 14–15 on a randomized decision rule sampled from a conditional action law. The stated equal-risk consequence is outside the current inventory.

contents.name: Slides 14–15: a randomized rule is specified by a conditional probability distribution on actions
contents.reason: This is an independent construction example; the local definition supplies the full measurable-kernel conditions that these slides leave implicit.

contents.name: Slides 14–15: randomization preserves the risk after a sufficiency reduction
contents.reason: That result is not part of this pair and requires a sufficiency setup; it is not used to prove the definition or action-law lemma.
